Subject: Intermittent stalls to private deployment during peak — initial report

Hi Neha,

We're seeing intermittent stalls and retransmits when our clients talk to the private deployment endpoints (10.12.x.x) over the managed VPN during peak hours. Small requests (short payloads) look fine, but larger payloads (~1.5–2MB responses) often hang and then succeed after multiple retransmits.

What we've captured so far:
- TCP retransmit bursts and occasional MSS-clamp signatures in the pcap.
- Traceroute shows a single handoff through the ClearHarbor VPN gateway to Redwood's edge (attached).
- When we temporarily lower application payloads to ~600KB, failures stop.

We attached a short pcap and traceroute. Can you confirm whether there's any MTU/MSS clamp or NAT state behavior on the Redwood side that would drop large packets or reset ephemeral sessions?

Attachments: clearharbor-pcap-20260731.pcap (pcap), traceroute-20260731.txt

Thanks,
Laura Cheng

Subject: Re: Intermittent stalls to private deployment during peak — conntrack + early analysis

Quick update after an initial look at the pcap and edge state (conntrack dump attached). Observations:
- Multiple sessions showed SNAT port reuse where the original ephemeral port is reused for a different 5-tuple after conntrack expiry. That correlates with the "hang then resume" pattern when clients re-establish.
- There are several "ICMP fragmentation needed" messages in the capture, but our edge is not currently doing MSS clamping on the VPN tunnel. If the customer tunnel or an intermediate hop is smaller than 1500 MTU, large packets may be dropped and TCP only recovers after retransmit.
- Conntrack entries for some flows are expiring earlier than expected due to high ephemeral port churn during bursts; we see a few entries with TTLs that went to zero unexpectedly.

Next proposed checks:
1) Enable MSS clamp at the tunnel endpoint (temporary) on our edge and ask ClearHarbor to do the same on their VPN gateway.
2) Temporarily widen allowed ephemeral source port range in security groups to rule out SG blocking after SNAT translation.
3) Collect sFlow for the period of the reproductions to confirm path MTUs. I've attached a quick conntrack dump: conntrack_dump_20260801.txt and sflow snapshot sflow_snapshot_20260801.txt.

I can be on the call at 09:00 PT.

—Marcus

Date: Sat, 01 Aug 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent stalls to private deployment during peak — SG and ACL review

Adding a security perspective. I checked the per-tenant security groups applied at the private edge. Current SG for this tenant restricts ingress to a narrow set of ports and only explicitly lists ephemeral ports 49152-49160 (leftover from an older NAT design). That will definitely cause drops if SNAT rewrites the source port into a port outside that tiny range.

Immediate mitigations I recommend: 
- Temporarily allow 32768-61000 on the tenant SG for TCP ingress from the ClearHarbor gateway CIDR.
- Apply an MSS clamp set to 1400 on the Redwood tunnel interface to avoid 1500->(smaller path) issues.
- After mitigation and confirmation, we'll narrow the range and document port-mapping expectations in the private deployment onboarding docs.

I'll push the SG change as a short-lived exception (load-controlled) if sponsors approve. Laura — please confirm if you can set MSS clamp on your side or if we should do a path-based MTU minimization instead.

—Vanessa

Subject: Re: Intermittent stalls to private deployment during peak — results from test

Thanks for the quick triage. We made two temporary changes on our side this morning during the 09:00 PT test window:
1) Enabled MSS clamp 1400 on the ClearHarbor VPN gateway.
2) Confirmed our egress preserves ephemeral ports in the 32768-61000 range (no pooling).

Results:
- After MSS clamp, large responses no longer hang during the test — throughput improved and retransmits dropped by ~95%.
- We still see occasional short stalls when traffic bursts coincide with high NAT churn on Redwood's edge (one or two retransmits).

Attached is our VPN gateway config excerpt: vpn-config-20260802.txt. Luke from NetworkWorks also confirmed the path MTU between their gateway and Redwood's edge shows an MTU of 1404 on one intermediate hop (hence the need for MSS clamp).

Next asks from our side: can Redwood make the MSS clamp change on the private edge as a coordinated, short-lived config so we can remove the clamp on our side and validate symmetric behavior? Also, can you confirm whether a change in conntrack/TTL policy would be safe (Marcus suggested entries are expiring early)?

Appreciate the help.

—Laura

Thanks everyone for fast triage and the test results. Summary and action items: 

Summary:
- Root cause contributor: intermediate hop with MTU ~1404 causing large packets to require MSS clamping. Secondary contributor: narrow tenant SG and aggressive conntrack expiry leading to SNAT port reuse and transient stalls.

Action plan (owners and timeline):
- Vanessa: Apply temporary SG exception to allow 32768-61000 for ClearHarbor CIDR (expires 48h) — actioned now and PR created (JIRA-RED-1427).
- Marcus: Apply MSS clamp 1400 on the Redwood tunnel interface for the tenant and increase conntrack timeout for established flows to reduce premature expiry. Schedule: change window 03 Aug 2026 02:00–03:00 PT; rollback plan included in playbook.
- Karthik & Monica: Update private deployment onboarding docs with explicit NAT/SG expectations and a checklist for MSS/clamp and MTU validation. Linked playbook: https://redwood.internal/playbooks/private-connectivity-vpn-mtu
- Neha: Coordinate a validation window with ClearHarbor (prefer 03 Aug 09:00 PT) and confirm whether ClearHarbor removes their MSS clamp after our change for symmetric validation.

Laura — can you confirm availability for the 03 Aug 09:00 PT test? If you prefer earlier we can try 08:00. Also attaching the internal conntrack dump and sflow snapshots we used.

I'll follow up with a post-change summary and a short root-cause write-up for the account.

Best regards,
